subject: AcmeCorp — security/compliance follow-up & subprocessor list
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmecorp.com>, Sara Kim <s.kim@acme.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 5 Jun 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: AcmeCorp discovery recap — security requests and next steps

Hi Jordan / Sara,

Thanks again for the time today — really helpful to understand AcmeCorp's primary inference workloads and data residency needs. Quick recap and next steps from our side: 

- Primary ask from your security team: SOC 2 status (Type II report if available) and current list of subprocessors (cloud providers + any third-party vendors that process customer data).
- You mentioned GDPR applicability for EU users and potential HIPAA-scope for a subset of records — want to confirm which dataset categories are PHI so we can scope controls and a potential BAA.
- Neha (SE) will follow up on architecture questions and example request/response flows to validate data boundaries.

Could you share the current subprocessor list and let us know whether AcmeCorp prefers a short-form asset (CSV/PDF) or the full vendor security questionnaire? If you already have vendor questionnaire answers, feel free to attach them.

Attachments from our side: I've attached a one-pager that outlines typical subprocessor categories and the standard info customers request (redwood-subprocessors-2027-06.pdf) and a short SOC2 FAQ.

Proposed next steps:
1) Share subprocessor list + any vendor questionnaire (Jordan) — by EOD Mon 6/7 if possible.
2) Neha to send architecture diagram and sample flows by Tue 6/8.
3) Intro call with our security lead (Aditya) if your team wants to review controls — available next week.

Thanks — Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0132

From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmecorp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sara Kim <s.kim@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AcmeCorp discovery recap — security requests and next steps

Hi Marissa — thanks for the recap and for the helpful one-pager.

Attached is our initial subprocessor list (high-level) and the vendor security questionnaire (we've filled the basics but left a couple of items for the vendor to complete). We can provide the full questionnaire if Redwood can return the answers as part of the standard procurement review.

Quick notes:
- Our primary cloud providers: AWS (us-east-1), Google Cloud (us-west1) for analytics pipelines. We treat inference outputs as customer data; we have strict egress controls to prevent downstream sharing.
- SOC 2: We maintain SOC 2 Type II reports internally and can share an executive summary during the procurement phase — need an NDA before the full report.
- HIPAA: A small subset of records are PHI; we expect vendors to sign a BAA for any PHI processing.

Attaching: acme-subprocessors-2027-06.csv, acme-vendor-questionnaire-partial.xlsx

Can you confirm Redwood's approach to subprocessors (what categories are included) and whether you support BAAs? If possible, please have your security lead call Aditya and Rishi's team to align on the BAA and SOC2 exchange process.

Thanks,
Jordan

--
Jordan Lee
Director, IT Security | AcmeCorp
jordan.lee@acmecorp.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: AcmeCorp discovery recap — security requests and next steps

Aditya / Rishi — forwarding Jordan's response and the partial questionnaire. High-level asks:

- Shareable subprocessor list (Jordan attached CSV) — need to confirm which of our subprocessors we can disclose and at what granularity.
- SOC 2: Jordan says they need an NDA before the full report; they can share an exec summary earlier.

- BAA: They expect vendors to sign a BAA for PHI processing.

Questions for you:
1) Can we share our subprocessor list at the service-category level (e.g., cloud provider: AWS/GCP, analytics: Segment, monitoring: Datadog) or do we need to provide vendor legal names?
2) Do we currently sign BAAs for customers who require HIPAA coverage? If yes, what is the typical timeline and any legal-preferred language?
3) Do we need to provide a SOC 2 executive summary or is the SOC 2 status on our public security page sufficient for procurement teams?

Neha: please take the action to map their stated cloud regions (us-east-1, us-west1) to our deployment options and confirm any data residency implications.

Thanks — Marissa

>

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: AcmeCorp discovery recap — security requests and next steps

Marissa / team — thanks for the ping and for the attachments. Quick answers and proposed next steps below.

1) Subprocessor disclosure: We maintain a public, customer-facing subprocessor list that discloses vendors at the legal entity level and primary service category. For procurement, customers often request a downloadable CSV/PDF with legal names — we can provide that. For highly sensitive partners we redact specifics until an NDA is signed, but AWS/GCP (cloud infra), Datadog (monitoring) and our caching/CDN providers are fine to disclose. I'll attach our canonical subprocessor export.

2) BAA / HIPAA: Yes, we support BAAs for customers in scope. Standard timeline: 2-3 weeks for legal review (often faster with standard template). We have a boilerplate BAA we can share; legal prefers a brief initial review before signing.

3) SOC 2: We have a SOC 2 Type II in progress for the 2026–2027 cycle. We can provide an executive summary to procurement prior to an NDA and provide the full report under NDA. Our public security page lists the current SOC 2 status and scope.

Next steps (proposed):
- I'll attach our consumable subprocessor list (redwood-subprocessors-2027-06.pdf) and SOC2-FAQ.pdf for Jordan.
- Marissa: please share the acme-subprocessors-2027-06.csv you attached; we'll map any discrepancies.
- Recommend a 30-min sync between Jordan + Acme procurement and our security team (Aditya + Rishi) — availability Wed 6/9 10:00–12:00 PT or Thu 6/10 14:00–16:00 PT.

If you want, I can also complete the vendor questionnaire an initial pass for the security controls section to accelerate procurement.

Thanks — Aditya

--
Aditya Rao
Security Lead | Redwood Inference
